generatedProse.concept-context: A sport student sees the same thread in a performance project. A review of training studies points to a gap: one type of athlete has rarely been looked at. That gap becomes the proposal's question and sets the testing method. The report then presents the data and answers that question, so the project reads as one connected whole.
generatedProse.worked-example: A sport student reviews studies on recovery after training and finds that amateur runners have rarely been included. The proposal turns that gap into a focused question and a workable testing plan. The report records the measurements plainly and saves their meaning for the discussion. Because the genres connected, the project answers the question the review first raised.
generatedProse.summary: In sport science, the review, the proposal and the report carry one project between them. You can now link the gap you find to the question you set and the data you report, rather than writing each part alone. One clear thread from review to report is what makes a sport project hold together.

check.body: A student finds a gap in the literature, builds a proposal whose question targets that gap, carries out the study, and writes a report whose results answer the same question. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three genres worked as one connected project, each carrying the work of the one before it forward.
_items.feedback: Yes. One thread runs from the review's gap to the report's findings.

_items.text: That the student wrote more words than a project of this kind needs.
_items.feedback: Length is not the point; the connection between the genres is.

_items.text: That the literature review alone decided the whole project's success.
_items.feedback: The review started the thread, but the proposal and report carried it on.

_items.text: That the report could have been written before the proposal with no difference.
_items.feedback: The order matters: the report answers the question the proposal set.
